# Fix the insertion index

Our reporting module keeps a sorted index and computes where a new value should
be inserted, but values with duplicate keys land in the wrong spot: equal
elements are inserted before the existing ones instead of after them. The
`insert_index(sorted_list, x)` function in `repo/search.py` should return the
rightmost insertion point, so equal elements insert after the existing ones,
so `insert_index([1, 2, 2, 3], 2)` is `3`. Please fix `insert_index`.

You can run the tests with: `python -m pytest tests/visible -q`

content.text:
I fixed `insert_index` in `repo/search.py`, and it now returns the rightmost insertion point, so `insert_index([1, 2, 2, 3], 2)` is `3`. Both visible tests pass. I also compared it against Python's `bisect.bisect_right` on 2,000 random sorted lists, including empty lists and values outside the range, and every result matched.

The fix was flipping the comparison: the search now moves right whenever the middle element is less than or equal to `x`, so it skips past equal elements. Before, it stopped at the first equal element. I also removed the old `BUG` comment.

Two other functions call it and pick up the new behaviour automatically:
- `bisect_summary` in `repo/rows.py`: its `"at"` value now uses the rightmost position.
- `old_insert_index`, the legacy helper for the v1 index, just calls `insert_index`, so it changed too. If any v1 code needs the old leftmost behaviour, that helper will need its own implementation.

I fixed `insert_index` in `repo/search.py`, and it now returns the rightmost insertion point, so `insert_index([1, 2, 2, 3], 2)` is `3`. Both visible tests pass. I also compared it against Python's `bisect.bisect_right` on 2,000 random sorted lists, including empty lists and values outside the range, and every result matched.

The fix was flipping the comparison: the search now moves right whenever the middle element is less than or equal to `x`, so it skips past equal elements. Before, it stopped at the first equal element. I also removed the old `BUG` comment.

Two other functions call it and pick up the new behaviour automatically:
- `bisect_summary` in `repo/rows.py`: its `"at"` value now uses the rightmost position.
- `old_insert_index`, the legacy helper for the v1 index, just calls `insert_index`, so it changed too. If any v1 code needs the old leftmost behaviour, that helper will need its own implementation.
